sentences.sentence: Finish a game, then start another one during a mismatch.
Finish every supported size with complete pairs.
Reveal one card twice, then reveal a different card. Check the exact move count.
Match a pair, then miss a pair. Check the immediate match and the 800ms active mismatch interval.
Hide the page during a mismatch, then return and finish its remaining interval.
Start and restart during a mismatch. Check the cleared state and later timer updates.
Finish games with better, equal and worse move counts. Reload and check the current size's best.
Use pointer, touch and keyboard to follow [Input](input.md) and [Controls](controls.md).
Check control labels, row movement, edge stops, native Tab exit and focus after each action.
Check that hidden cards reveal no identity in the DOM.
Follow the keyboard journey in I17 and check its accessibility tree.
During user acceptance, confirm spoken results with a screen reader, including consecutive identical results and the final match with its win.
Measure the layout and review all 128 faces against [Visuals](visuals.md).
Use a 44px grayscale face sheet to distinguish shape, marker and fill.
Check 16x16 boards at both stated viewport sizes, full focus outlines and the equivalent zoom layout.
Check reduced motion and the static completion banner after its single pulse.
Play through completion and reset while checking [Sound](sound.md). Every action stays silent.
Check [Reproducibility](reproducibility.md) with its example deck and replay.
Check snapshot round trips and malformed input.
Check the exact mismatch timeout before an equal-time replay action.
Load an unfinished snapshot, attempt input while paused, then Resume. Check its remaining active time and focus.
Load a completed snapshot and check its static banner and unchanged best score.
Use a locked install, type check, unit tests and a fresh browser build as defined in [Technology](technology.md).
Open the resulting HTML directly from disk with network access blocked.
Use a local HTTP origin for saved preferences.
Review the pure game functions, browser effects, file sizes and behavior placement against [Architecture](architecture.md).
Model game data with readonly interfaces and named discriminated unions.
A filesystem dependency belongs in replay's command wrapper, not in a browser rule function.
Use the main Vite configuration for both the development entry and production game build.
A future build-tool change would have to preserve the distribution and command behavior; the current game model is not tied to Vite APIs.
An algorithm change would need a different generation version.
Export progress as readable version 1 JSON.
Matched positions must be unique, in range and form whole face pairs.
A pending mismatch needs two different unmatched positions whose faces differ, with remaining time from 1 through 800 whole milliseconds.
Moves must cover the matched pairs and a pending mismatch.
A started game with zero moves needs its first revealed card.
Use `performance.now()` in the browser session adapter and pass measured positive deltas to the game.
Whole-millisecond representation belongs at export.
An action therefore must not assume that the last rendered elapsed value is the current active time.
Use Vitest for focused tests under `src` and `scripts`.
Fixtures and expected values need to remain independent enough to detect regressions.
A functional fix still needs the evidence appropriate to that behavior.
An update still needs current evidence, and a lockfile can faithfully reproduce a flawed combination.
A stored best also cannot be lower than the board's pair count, because even perfect play needs one move per pair.
The restart case is particularly important: an old timer must not close a newly revealed card in the restarted deal.
The size rules that are explicit concern authored TypeScript files: an aim of 100 lines and a ceiling of 200 lines per file.
A string constructed from pair count still needs correct grammar; the first matched pair and later pairs use different forms.
Replay actions are processed in their array order, with logical time advanced to each action's `atMs` before activating its card. Times must be nondecreasing.
Conversely, a changed generation algorithm cannot hide behind a release tag while continuing to give the same board-code prefix a different meaning.
Keep the product specification with the project so a behavior change can be understood alongside its implementation and evidence.
The product specification belongs in `docs/` alongside the source.
The source-size specification aims for 100 lines per TypeScript file and limits authored files to 200 lines.
New stored data uses a key of the form np3:THING, where THING is a lowercase plural noun for what is stored. Keys that already exist keep their names.
The page has exactly one live region, the status paragraph in Game.tsx. New status text, such as whose turn it is, goes through that region.

Keep deck generation, card transitions, logical time, snapshot validation and replay as pure functions under `src/game`. They receive their inputs directly. They don't read the DOM, storage, external random sources or browser clocks.
Keep the board description and deck immutable.
Keep matched positions, current selection, moves, active elapsed milliseconds and whether play started in game state.
Derive pair count and victory.
Serialize progress using the [reproducibility formats](reproducibility.md).
Use direct calls and exhaustive branches for the closed, one-card and mismatch states.
Keep named states, format versions, timing values and size limits beside the behavior they control.
Keep React state, timer lifecycle and browser visibility handling in `src/game/session`.
Use a monotonic browser clock.
Clear pending work on unmount and invalidate callbacks when the deal changes.
A callback from an earlier deal can't change the current one.
Keep preference and best-score reads in the session storage module.
Treat saved JSON as unknown input.
Validate grid sizes and finite integer scores.
Catch read, parse and write failures. Keep unrelated storage keys untouched. A failure leaves the game playable.
Keep active game progress in memory until you export or import a snapshot.
Importing a completed snapshot doesn't update best scores or play a celebration.
Completing an unfinished imported game records a local best under R10.
`Game.tsx` composes status, the board, game controls and reproduction controls.
Keep board navigation in `src/game/board`, controls in `src/game/controls` and session behavior in `src/game/session`.
Keep each component's props and styles beside it.
A card mounts its face SVG only while revealed or matched.
Hidden card identity stays out of DOM attributes, accessible names and diagnostic globals.
Tests can know a deck from its documented board code. The app gives them no solver endpoint.
Use native browser input and the shared card activation function.
Keep focus position in the board component.
Focus movement changes presentation, never the deck or move count.
Keep focused tests beside their behavior.
Complete browser journeys live at the application test level.
Check generation against independent literal vectors.
Check game transitions against stated rules.
Test built HTML from disk as well as served storage behavior.
Keep development fixtures and diagnostic helpers out of the shipped game.
The shipped game exposes only its documented controls.
Add a new rule at its game behavior, then update its component, tests and specification.
Add shared support only when two actual behaviors need the same meaning.
Don't add a global store, event bus, router or generic utility folder.
A port to a language with narrower integer multiplication needs to preserve the same arithmetic rather than relying on overflowing 32-bit products.
A change that alters arrangements needs a generation-version decision rather than a cosmetic refactor label.
A successful unflagged run can supply evidence for its actual combination; it cannot be relabeled as a named-combination pass if the values differ.
A future compatibility result for another engine would need to distinguish portable journeys from Chromium-specific evidence.
For a release, use the complete build-and-run command and interpret failures with their environment and fixture availability.
The architecture specification calls for adding a rule at its game behavior and updating its component, tests and specification.
State is never shown by color alone, so a winner is marked with the text "(winner)" after the name.
Quarterfinals are played on 4x4, semifinals on 6x6 and finals on 8x8.
Both players of a match play one board code, and every match in a tournament has a different board code.
Seeds follow entry order, so the first player entered is seed 1.
A bracket of four meets as 1 against 4, then 2 against 3.
A bracket of eight meets as 1 against 8, 4 against 5, 3 against 6, then 2 against 7.
Name each round Quarterfinal, Semifinal or Final, and show it as "Round: NAME" while that round is played.
A bracket of four has no Quarterfinal.
Tournament games never change best scores or the saved board size.
Competition adds no extra points, multiplier or group total.
When both players of a match finish in the same number of moves, the lower active time wins, and if that is also equal the higher seed wins. Seed 1 is the highest seed.
Label the native size select "Grid size". Give it options `4x4`, `6x6`, `8x8`, `10x10`, `12x12`, `14x14` and `16x16`, with numeric side length `N` as each value.
After a successful board-code or snapshot load, select the loaded board's size.
Label the fresh-deal button "New Game". It creates a fresh seed and keeps the current size.
Label the repeat-deal button "Restart". It starts the same board code again.
Changing size, starting and restarting follow the session rules in [Rules](rules.md).
Put reproduction controls inside a native `details` element that starts collapsed. Give its summary the exact text "Reproduce a game".
The controls use the board-code and snapshot formats defined in [Reproducibility](reproducibility.md).
Label the text input "Board code" and limit it to 32 characters.
Show the current board code after a new deal, Restart or a successful load.
Keep an edited draft when a card action changes the game.
Label its button "Load board". Validate the entered code before replacing the current game with that deal's starting state.
Label the textarea "Snapshot JSON" and limit it to 65536 characters. The parser also applies the UTF-8 byte limit in the snapshot format.
Label the export button "Export snapshot".
Fill the textarea with readable version 1 snapshot JSON that you can select and copy manually.
Export leaves the game state and clock unchanged. It requires no Clipboard API.
Export `elapsedMs` and a pending mismatch's `remainingMs` as whole milliseconds.
A pending mismatch always exports at least 1ms.
Label the import button "Load snapshot". Validate the complete draft before replacing the current game.
Load unfinished progress paused and show "Loaded snapshot. Select Resume to continue."
Load completed progress as completed without pausing and show "Loaded completed snapshot."
Show a "Resume" button only while an imported unfinished game is paused. Selecting it clears that pause. Unfinished play continues from the loaded state.
While paused, block every card activation and allow board focus movement.
On Resume, move focus to the board's remembered tab stop before removing the Resume button.
A loaded completed game stays completed and shows no Resume button.

On invalid input, keep the current game and the entered draft for correction. Show the exact status for that control:

| Control | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Load board | Invalid board code. |
| Load snapshot | Invalid snapshot. |
A loaded completed snapshot keeps the win banner static and plays no celebration. Import doesn't write a best score.
Resuming an unfinished snapshot and later winning records a local best under R10.
Keep focus on the button used for starting, restarting, loading or exporting. These actions don't move focus to the board.
Resume follows C10 because its button disappears. The board's remembered tab stop follows the focus rules in [Input](input.md#focus).
Keep replay in the developer CLI and game core. V1 has no replay controls in the game UI.
Run `npm run --silent replay -- PATH` to read a replay file.
On valid input, print only the final snapshot JSON to stdout and exit 0.
On invalid input, print nothing to stdout, write a message to stderr and exit nonzero.
A stored value that fails to parse or validate is treated as empty, without any error, and stays untouched until the next save replaces it.

Every new exported JSON object has a "format" of "neon-pairs/KIND", naming what it holds, and a whole-number "version", with its keys in alphabetical order at every level. Formats that already exist stay as they are.
A feature adds no entries to dependencies or devDependencies.
Leaving unfinished work asks first in a native dialog element with two buttons, Keep playing and Leave. Keep playing takes focus when it opens, and Escape keeps playing.
Names in one group compare without regard to case, after normalization. A repeat blocks the action and shows "Each name must be different."
Export must include all active time and the correct pending interval.
When a feature replaces what the main area shows, focus moves to that screen's h2, which has tabindex="-1".
The reproducibility specification explicitly ties `np1` to the generation algorithm and says that a generation change requires another version.
An import with a field its format doesn't define shows "Unknown field: NAME." for the first such field and leaves the current state unchanged.
Render each card as a native button. A primary click, a completed tap, Enter and Space activate the card through the same action.
Keep the browser's normal context menu on right-click or long-press. Opening that menu doesn't activate a card.
Hover and pointer cancellation leave the game state unchanged.
Give the board one remembered tab stop. When Tab enters the board, focus that card. Use the first card before any board focus has been remembered.

Move focus with these keys. Movement changes focus without activating a card:

| Key | Focus destination |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowLeft | Previous card in the same row |
| ArrowRight | Next card in the same row |
| ArrowUp | Card in the previous row and same column |
| ArrowDown | Card in the next row and same column |

The board handles only these four arrow keys without modifiers, plus Enter and Space. It leaves every other key and modifier combination to the browser and doesn't use them to move focus or activate a card.
Stop arrow movement at a board edge.
Let native Tab and Shift+Tab leave the board. Moving through the board uses the movement keys instead of adding every card to the page's tab order.
Keep matched cards focusable and mark them `aria-disabled="true"`. Their game action follows the matched-card rule in the gameplay document.
While a mismatching pair waits to turn back, allow focus movement and block card activation.
On initial load, keep the browser's current focus. Loading the game doesn't move focus to the board.
After a new deal, Restart or a successful load, reset the board's remembered tab stop to its first card.

When a card receives focus, scroll it into view with nearest alignment in the board's scroll area. Give each card a scroll margin of at least 6px, so its complete focus outline stays in view, including mid-board cards.
The session buttons keep their focus as defined in [Controls](controls.md).
Name a hidden card by its one-based row, column and closed state. Keep its face SVG and face identifier out of the DOM while it is hidden, including attributes and accessible text.
Name a revealed or matched card by its position, face name and state. Use the face names defined in [Visuals](visuals.md).
Use one polite, atomic live region for turn results and completion.
Announce each turn result exactly once.
A winning turn has one announcement containing both the match and the win.
Consecutive identical results each get their own announcement.
Focus movement, clock renders and closing a mismatch don't repeat a result.

Use these turn announcements, where `M` is the matched pair count, `N` is moves and `time` uses R07's display format:

| Event | Announcement |
| --- | --- |
| First match | Pair found. 1 pair matched. |
| Later match | Pair found. M pairs matched. |
| Miss | No match. Cards close after a short pause. |
| Final match | Pair found. All pairs found in N moves and time. |
Send the load statuses in Controls through this same live region once per load event. Keep the visible status beside the reproduction controls.

Support a complete 4x4 keyboard game with a screen reader. Find Grid size and New Game by name, enter the board, expose closed positions and revealed faces by name and state, announce one result per turn and make the win, final moves and time available. Leave the board with Tab and start another game. Deliver automated accessibility-tree evidence for this journey.
Record the browser and tool versions in the project README and say whether a screen reader was used. If one was used, record its name and version.
The user confirms spoken output during acceptance. Spoken confirmation isn't the developer's deliverable.
Any future spoken test result would need to identify the actual browser and screen reader used rather than inheriting the current tree-only record.
A command working under another supported Node version needs its own evidence before that version can be described as tested.
A feature lives in src/game/FEATURE/, and its rules live in src/game/FEATURE/rules.ts, which imports neither React nor any browser global.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, new elements run no animation and no transition.
A name has 2 to 20 Unicode code points after normalization. Anything else blocks the action and shows "Use 2 to 20 characters."
Counts of moves read "1 move" and "2 moves", and durations read M:SS, such as 0:07 and 12:30.
Replacing generation for speed still has to preserve the version 1 deal.
An overdue mismatch must resolve before the next valid reveal is considered.
Every value a feature adds to browser storage is a JSON object with exactly two keys: "v", the number 3, and "items", the array of records.
Only src/game/session/fresh-board.ts may call a random source. Everything else that needs randomness imports it from there.
The snapshot unit suite checks export after 0.75ms of a miss and again with 0.25ms left. The result must decode successfully and remain within one millisecond of the active state.
Identify the source being released and use a complete writable checkout for commands that install, build or write test artifacts.
Read the current specification and [Acceptance](acceptance.md), especially the journey affected by the change.
Check that reviewed test inputs are present.
Inspect the package and lockfile together.
Do not infer a format migration from the product specification number alone; [Format versioning](format-versioning-guide.md) explains that distinction.
Read the generated runtime record to establish what launched.
Finish by stopping any development servers or watchers started for the work.
Preserve the concrete test result and runtime information used for the release record.
Use `np1-N-seed`, where `N` is a supported side length and `seed` is an integer from `1` through `2147483646`. Use decimal digits without leading zeros. The parser accepts exactly this form.
Trim surrounding whitespace in the Board code control before parsing.

Version `np1` fixes the generation algorithm below. The same code produces the same deck in every supported runtime. Changing generation requires another version. Time, animation and other random draws can't change this deck.
Start the Park-Miller generator at `state = seed`. Each draw sets `state = (state * 16807) % 2147483647`. Use exact integer arithmetic.
Create the deck as `[0, 0, 1, 1, ...]` through face `N * N / 2 - 1`. Shuffle from index `N * N - 1` down to `1`. At index `i`, draw `j` in `0..i` and swap positions `i` and `j`.
For a draw with `b` possible results, set `q = 2147483646` and `limit = floor(q / b) * b`. Advance the generator and set `x = state - 1`. If `x >= limit`, draw again. Otherwise return `x % b`.

Encode progress as a JSON object with exactly `version`, `boardCode`, `matched`, `selection`, `moves`, `elapsedMs` and `started`. `version` is `1`. `matched` is an array of matched position indices. Derive the deck, pair count and completion from these fields.

The `selection` object has one of these forms:

| `kind` | Other fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `closed` | None | No unmatched card is revealed |
| `one` | `index` | One unmatched card is revealed |
| `mismatch` | `first`, `second`, `remainingMs` | Two different faces await closing |
Validate the complete object before replacing the game. Reject unknown keys.
Require unique in-range matched indices containing whole face pairs.
Selection indices must be in range and unmatched.
A mismatch needs distinct indices with different faces and an integer `remainingMs` from `1` through `800`.
Completion requires a closed selection.
Require boolean `started` and nonnegative safe integers for `moves` and `elapsedMs`. Reject `elapsedMs` above `359999999` and `moves` above `999999`. Apply the move cap to saved best scores too.
Require at least one move per matched pair and one further move for a pending mismatch.
If `started` is false, require zero moves, zero elapsed time, no matches and a closed selection.
A started game with zero moves requires one revealed card.
Import of unfinished progress pauses the clock and pending mismatch until Resume.
Completed imports stay completed without a pause.

Encode a single deal as `{version: 1, boardCode, actions: [{atMs, index}], endMs}`. Require exactly these fields and exactly `atMs` and `index` per action. Indices must be in range. Times are nonnegative safe integers. Action times must be nondecreasing. If actions exist, `endMs` must be at least the final action time. Equal-time actions keep array order.
Start from the code's hidden deal. Advance active time to each action's `atMs` before activating its index, then advance to `endMs`.
Resolve a mismatch whose interval ends exactly at an action time before that action.
Apply the game rules to ignored activation too.
Cap replayed elapsed time at `359999999` milliseconds as R07 requires.
Action times and `endMs` keep the nonnegative safe integer range in D08.
Limit snapshot JSON to `65536` UTF-8 bytes.
Limit replay JSON to `1048576` UTF-8 bytes and `10000` actions.

Reject malformed JSON and unsupported format versions. For snapshots, inconsistent data means a violation of D05, D06 or D07. For replays, it means a violation of D08 or D09. For board codes, validate D01. Validation checks these stated constraints, without requiring a reconstructed history of earlier turns.
Invalid board codes and snapshots keep the current browser game.
Invalid replay files are rejected by the CLI and game core.
These local formats and saved scores are untrusted input. Validation checks the state rules, not a verified play history.
A stored list keeps its newest 10 records and drops older ones when a new record is saved.
A turn reveals two eligible cards.
A match adds one pair, while a miss gives you time to remember the faces before both cards turn back.
Support square boards with side lengths `4`, `6`, `8`, `10`, `12`, `14` and `16`.
Every face occurs exactly twice.
Positions run from zero in row order.
The deal comes from the board code defined in [Reproducibility](reproducibility.md).
The first valid card activation reveals that card. Activating it again or activating a matched card has no game effect.
The next valid activation reveals a different unmatched card. If the two faces match, keep them revealed and add one matched pair immediately.

If the faces differ, show both for `800` active milliseconds, then close both together. Ignore all card activation during this interval. Pause the interval while the page is hidden or an imported snapshot awaits Resume.
Add one move when the second valid card is revealed.
The first reveal and ignored activation add no moves.
Matches and misses each cost one move until the count reaches `999999`. At that cap the count stops increasing. Play continues normally, pairs still match and the game still completes.
Show the current move count throughout play as `Moves: N`.
Give one point per matched pair and no other score.
Show matched pairs against the board's total pairs throughout play as `Pairs: M/T`, where `M` is matched pairs and `T` is the total.
Complete the game when every pair is matched.
Show the final moves and elapsed time with a completion banner.
Apply the completion motion defined in [Visuals](visuals.md).
Start elapsed time on the first valid reveal. Count active milliseconds while the page is shown. Pause while the page is hidden or an imported snapshot awaits Resume. Stop at completion.
Rendering frequency doesn't change the elapsed time.
Cap elapsed time at `359999999` milliseconds. At the cap, play continues normally and the clock shows the capped time.
Show the clock throughout play as `Time: m:ss`.
Round elapsed seconds down, pad seconds to two digits and let minutes continue past 59.
The mismatch interval and elapsed clock use the same active time. Showing the page again continues the interval from its remaining time.
Start with `4` rows and `4` columns unless a saved supported size exists.
Remember the last chosen size after reload.
A page load starts a fresh deal.
Loading a valid board code or snapshot also saves its size as the last chosen size.
A failed load keeps the saved size unchanged.

New Game creates a fresh seed at the current size. Restart keeps the current board code. Choosing a different size creates a fresh seed at that size. Each action clears the selection, matched pairs, moves and elapsed time.

When play completes a game, keep its moves if they beat the saved best for that size. Keep these records after reload. An equal or worse result keeps the existing best. Starting or restarting a game keeps these records.
Show the current size's best move count throughout play and after completion as `Best: N`. Before that size has a record, show `Best: none`.
Invalid board codes and snapshots show an error and keep the current game.
Invalid saved preferences are ignored.
If storage is unavailable, play continues without saving.
Starting, restarting, replacing or leaving a game invalidates its pending timer updates.
An update from an earlier game or turn can't change the current game.
Keep the game silent for every action and state, including a reveal, a match, a mismatch, a restart and a win.
Include no audio files, audio API calls or sound toggle in this version.
When browser storage is blocked, a feature keeps working in memory and shows "Progress won't be saved on this device." where its saved records would appear.
Ranked or bracket data is a table element with a caption and th scope="col" header cells.
Every new control is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels at a 390 pixel wide viewport.
Use React with TypeScript and DOM rendering.
Use native buttons, a native select and CSS Grid.
Use no component library.

Pin these packages and keep the lockfile. The stable versions were checked on 31 October 2026:

| Package | Version | Job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `react`, `react-dom` | `19.3.1` | Browser UI |
| `typescript` | `7.0.2` | Type checking |
| `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom` | `19.3.0` | React types |

| `vitest` | `5.0.5` | Unit tests |
| `@playwright/test` | `1.64.1` | Browser tests |
| `@types/node` | `24.19.2` | Build and test types |
Use Node.js 24.19 or later and npm.
Keep browser and Node compiler projects separate.
Use ESM, static imports and type-only imports for types.

Use Node `26.12.1`, npm `11.20.0` and Playwright `1.64.1` with Chromium `156.0.8078.4` as the named compatibility combination. Record the locked install, build, unit tests and browser journeys with those exact versions in the project README before calling the combination tested. Other supported versions need their own results.
Enable TypeScript strictness, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` and `erasableSyntaxOnly`.
Keep type checking separate from bundling.
Model project data with exact types and validate unknown data where it enters the game.
Use narrowing instead of `any`, suppressed diagnostics or unchecked casts.
Derive state unions from their named values.
Keep behavior and its code, styles and tests together.
Aim for 100 lines per TypeScript file and keep authored TypeScript files at or below 200 lines.
Split by behavior when a file grows.
Use direct imports from the file that defines a behavior.

Provide these commands:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | Install the locked dependencies |
| `npm run dev` | Serve the game locally |
| `npm run typecheck` | Check every compiler project |
| `npm test` | Run unit tests for the game rules |
| `npm run test:e2e` | Build from current source, then run browser checks in fresh contexts against that build |
| `npm run build` | Type check and emit `dist/index.html` |
| `npm run --silent replay -- PATH` | Read replay JSON with the output and exit behavior in C14 |
The browser command must fail if its build fails. It must never fall back to an earlier `dist`.
Stop development servers and watchers you start before finishing the work.
`dist/index.html` contains the script, styles and artwork needed for play. It opens directly from disk without another file or a network request.
Use the system font.
Keep browser zoom enabled.
Serve the game from a local HTTP origin when checking saved preferences.
If storage is unavailable, play continues for the current session.
Keep dependencies in development and build tooling where possible.
The game uses no service, account, external asset, analytics or API key.
Dependency installation can use the network. Playing the distribution doesn't use it.
A feature's rules.ts has a rules.test.ts beside it.
A selected index must name an available position, a mismatch must involve different faces and complete matched pairs must be represented together.
Every name a person types is stored and shown after trimming both ends, collapsing each run of inner whitespace to one space and normalizing to NFC.
Game code reads time only through the session clock.
Only files in src/game/session/ may call performance.now, and no game code may use Date.
Run the tests in a complete writable checkout with their reviewed JSON inputs.
Use native controls and a CSS Grid board of DOM card buttons with inline SVG artwork.
Render the game without canvas.
Use no component library.
Center the content within a maximum width of 1120px and give it 16px padding.
Keep the outer page within the viewport width.
Limit the board's scroll area to `70dvh`, capped at 768px tall. Give it 6px padding and allow overflow on both axes inside that area.
Make each card square and size it from 44px to 88px according to the available board width.
Use a 6px grid gap, a 2px card border and an 8px card radius.
Fit the default four-column board within a phone viewport.
When a larger board reaches the 44px minimum card size, keep that size and scroll inside the board.

Use these colors for the page and controls:

| Token | Color | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page | `#090B14` | Page background |
| Panel | `#141827` | Board scroll area, reproduction panel and non-card button, select, input and textarea backgrounds |
| Back | `#1B2034` | Hidden card background |
| Face | `#111625` | Revealed card background |
| Text | `#F4F6FF` | Main text |
| Secondary | `#B8BDD2` | Help text, status labels and optional supporting text |
| Border | `#757C9A` | Neutral borders |
| Focus | `#FFFFFF` | Focus outline |

Use this ordered palette for card artwork:

| Index | Name | Color |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Cyan | `#63E7FF` |
| 1 | Magenta | `#FF71D6` |
| 2 | Green | `#8BEA7D` |
| 3 | Yellow | `#FFE082` |
| 4 | Orange | `#FFB064` |
| 5 | Violet | `#B49AFF` |
| 6 | Rose | `#FF8296` |
| 7 | Ice | `#D9F3FF` |
Use the system sans-serif font stack.
Set body text to 16px with a 24px line height, the title to 24px and secondary text to 14px. Secondary text means help text, status labels and optional supporting text.

Use spacing values of 4px, 6px, 8px, 12px, 16px, 24px and 32px for positive layout gaps, padding and margins you set. Allow zero resets and automatic centering. Reset browser default margins. Native control internals aren't covered. Card borders, radii, focus outlines, font metrics and SVG coordinates use their own stated values.

Generate 128 face identities from integer face IDs `0` through `127`. Calculate each face from these ordered values:

| Part | Calculation | Ordered values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shape | `id % 8` | Circle, square, triangle, diamond, star, hexagon, plus, chevron |
| Marker | `floor(id / 8) % 8` | Top, top-right, right, bottom-right, bottom, bottom-left, left, top-left |
| Fill | `floor(id / 64)` | Solid, outline |
| Color | Palette at marker index | The eight palette colors above |
Treat shape, marker and fill as the face identity. Color repeats the marker distinction and doesn't create a separate identity.
Draw each face in an SVG with `viewBox="0 0 100 100"`.
Center the main shape within `x=25..75` and `y=25..75`.
Draw the marker above the shape as a circle with radius 5, centered 40 units from `(50, 50)` in its marker direction.
Give the marker a 3-unit stroke in the Face background color, so it stays separate from the shape.
Normalize diagonal directions, giving offsets of about 28.284 units on each axis.
Use a 5-unit stroke for an outlined shape.
At 44px, all 128 identities must be distinguishable in a grayscale face sheet, including solid and outlined squares with diagonal markers.
Use the face color for the solid shape's fill, the outlined shape's stroke and the marker's fill. An outlined shape has no fill. The marker keeps its Face-background stroke.
Name each face with lowercase palette, fill, shape and marker names in the form "{color} {fill} {shape}, marker {position}".
Give every hidden card the same back with a neutral diamond.
Hidden cards keep their face artwork out of the DOM, as [Input](input.md#card-names) requires.
Show the face artwork on revealed cards. Keep it shown on matched cards and add a Green palette border and check mark.
Keep matched cards at full opacity.
Show keyboard focus with a 3px white outline offset by 2px.
Hover changes only the border to the Text color.
Matched cards keep their Green border when hovered.
Use a 120ms border-color transition. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, turn that transition off.

Show a win banner when the game finishes. Give it one 600ms pulse, then keep the banner static. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, show the static banner immediately. Use neither flashing nor confetti.

At viewport sizes 360x800 and 1280x800 CSS pixels, render all 256 cards of a 16x16 board. Keep the page within the viewport width and keep controls reachable. Keep each card at least 44px square, with scrolling confined to the board when needed. Reach the first and last card by touch scrolling and by keyboard. Scroll focused cards fully into view without clipping their focus outline.

At a 640x400 CSS-pixel viewport with device scale 2, the equivalent layout of 200% browser zoom from 1280x800, keep controls, status and the win summary readable without overlap. Keep the page within the viewport width. Keep both a 4x4 board and a 16x16 board playable with pointer and keyboard. Allow board scrolling and keep the focused card and its complete focus outline in view. Don't disable pinch zoom.
Interface text has no exclamation marks.
